policy-engines: Policy engines express allow/deny logic, evaluating a governance rule written as code and returning a machine-readable verdict tied to a commit, pull request or deploy.
policy-cards: Policy Cards are a proposed machine-readable, deployment-layer artefact that encodes an agent's operational, regulatory and ethical constraints and links them to enforcement and audit pipelines, so the rule travels with the agent as data.
registry: The agent registry is the runtime-aware inventory of every model, service and agent, each with an owner, a scope and a status, ideally written by the deployment pipeline rather than typed by hand.
discovery: Agent-discovery tools find AI the inventory did not know about and periodically reconcile the registry against what is actually running, flagging drift.
aibom: The AIBOM is the bill of materials for an AI system, recording models, datasets, weights and their provenance in CycloneDX ML-BOM or the SPDX 3.0 AI profile, generated at build and stored with the registry entry.
eval-frameworks: Evaluation frameworks run capability and regression suites in an eval gate wired into CI, so an eval below its agreed threshold fails the build and the release does not ship.
adversarial-probes: Adversarial and vulnerability probes run red-team evals against jailbreaks, prompt injection and tool misuse, producing the structured adversarial evidence the eval gate enforces.
guardrails: Guardrail frameworks are the runtime enforcement point where a policy fires against a live request, mediating tool calls and input/output for each agent.
observability: Observability builds on OpenTelemetry to trace and monitor agent runs, turning production behaviour into a control signal compared against the eval baseline.
agent-identity: Agent workload identity gives every non-human actor its own durable, attributable identity with a bounded scope and a tested kill switch that revokes access without breaking the fleet.
evidence-store: The assurance store holds machine-readable, audit-ready evidence emitted as OSCAL component and assessment artefacts, that any lower layer writes into and an auditor can read from.
assurance-suites: GRC and AI-governance suites aggregate and present the emitted evidence and generate framework mappings from it, so the audit becomes a query rather than a project.
